name: Anima (CircleStone Labs x Comfy Org)
publisher: CircleStone Labs in collaboration with Comfy Org; a derivative of NVIDIA Cosmos-Predict2-2B-Text2Image

architecture.what: 2B-parameter flow DiT built on Cosmos-Predict2-2B (ComfyUI detects it as a Cosmos Predict2 state dict with an llm_adapter); text encoder Qwen-3 0.6B base (qwen_3_06b_base, CLIPLoader); VAE the Qwen-Image VAE (qwen_image_vae, latent format Wan21); ComfyUI model class Anima: sampling shift 3.0, patch 2

cannot.what: realism / photographs: 'The model doesn't do realism well. This is intended.' — use a photoreal family
lengthy text: 'It can generally do single words and sometimes short phrases, but lengthy text rendering won't work well'
resolutions outside 512^2-1536^2 pixels ('Works at resolutions between 512^2 and 1536^2 pixels'); template note: 'weak high-res' — upscale after
a styled look from the base model alone: 'The default style is very plain and neutral, which is especially apparent if you don't use artist or quality tags'
image-to-image, inpainting or control in this knowledge base: only text-to-image recipes (the Anima LLLite control/inpaint templates, minComfyUIVersion 0.29.0, are not built here)

not_on_cloud.what: Anima-Aesthetic (v1.0, v1.0b, v1.1) and the full Anima-Turbo models (v1.0, v1.1) are published (HF split_files; Civitai model 2458426 as anima_aestheticV10/V11, anima_turboV10/V11) but are NOT in Comfy Cloud's UNETLoader list: a recreation of one brings it in the stage's `models` (folder diffusion_models, base 'Anima') and sets the unet_name port

lora.note: After the UNETLoader, before the KSampler — where the official base template puts its Turbo LoRA (LoraLoaderModelOnly). Core lora.py maps diffusion-model LoRA keys generically ('lora_unet_*' and plain 'diffusion_model.*' keys for every model) and names 'kohya anima' text-encoder LoRAs; LoraLoaderModelOnly patches the model only. Civitai tags Anima LoRAs 'Anima'. The card: LoRAs 'should be trained using' Anima-Base.

selection.why: the official Anima Base v1 template: 30 steps, cfg 4, euler/simple, 1024x1024 — the faithful default for anime / illustration work and for Anima images made with base-v1.0

selection.tradeoff: 8 steps at cfg 1 with the Turbo LoRA (the template's turbo switch); the card on distillation: 'increases stability and gives the model a strong default style, but reduces diversity'; the author 'recommend[s] starting with Anima-Turbo' for iterating on prompts

selection.why: the official preview template (anima-preview3-base, er_sde): RECREATE images made with the preview models (unet_name port: anima-preview3-base / anima-preview2 / anima-preview, all on Comfy Cloud)

rules.message: EmptyLatentImage takes width/height in multiples of 8 (node step 8)
the official template sizes Anima in multiples of 16 (ResolutionSelector multiple 16; the DiT patches the latent 2x2)
the card: 'Works at resolutions between 512^2 and 1536^2 pixels' (checked per side) — render inside it and upscale after
Anima encodes text with Qwen-3 0.6B base (qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors in a CLIPLoader, type stable_diffusion in the templates); ComfyUI's Anima clip target is that model
Anima decodes with the Qwen-Image VAE (qwen_image_vae.safetensors; latent format Wan21) — an SD/SDXL/FLUX VAE does not fit its latent
with the Turbo LoRA the official template sets cfg 1 (card, Anima-Turbo: 'Use at CFG 1')
with the Turbo LoRA the official template runs 8 steps (card, Anima-Turbo: '8-12 steps')
Anima-Turbo (the distilled model): 'Use at CFG 1 and 8-12 steps'
Anima-Turbo (the distilled model): 'Use at CFG 1 and 8-12 steps'
the card's generation settings: 'CFG 4-5' (the templates use 4); a recreation keeps the record's value
the card's generation settings: '30-50 steps' (the templates use 30); a recreation keeps the record's value
the recipe's template needs a newer ComfyUI than the pinned image (index.json minComfyUIVersion: base v1 0.16.0, preview 0.11.0)

prompting.negative_default: worst quality, low quality, score_1, score_2, score_3, blurry, jpeg artifacts, sepia
prompting.negative_gloss: the templates' negative; the card recommends 'worst quality, low quality, score_1, score_2, score_3, artist name, blurry, jpeg artifacts, chromatic aberration'. Aesthetic versions: no score_* tags in either prompt

positive.line: Trained on Danbooru-style tags, natural-language captions, and both mixed: 'Use lowercase for tags, and spaces instead of underscores. Score tags are the only tags that use underscores.'
Recommended positive prefix: 'masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, ' (the preview template opens with it; the base template prompt is plain natural language)

Quality tags: masterpiece … worst quality, and/or score_9 … score_1; time: 'year 2025', newest/recent/mid/early/old; meta: highres, absurdres, anime screenshot, official art; safety: safe, sensitive, nsfw, explicit
Artists need '@': '@big chungus' — 'The effect will be very weak if you don't'

Natural language: at least 2 sentences ('Extremely short prompts can give unexpected results'); name a character, then describe their appearance — 'extra important when prompting for multiple characters'
Weights work but need more than SDXL: '(chibi:2)'; Danbooru vs Gelbooru tag: prefer Gelbooru
Non-anime datasets: a first line 'ye-pop' or 'deviantart' (then optionally the alt-text / title on line 2) steers toward those styles

hurts.line: short, under-specified prompts without safety tags ('The model may generate undesired content, especially if the prompt is short or lacking details')
score_* tags on Anima-Aesthetic ('can push it too hard into slop territory')

pitfalls.symptom: plain, neutral, 'unstyled' images from the base model
pitfalls.cause: 'The base version is a true base model ... The default style is very plain and neutral'
pitfalls.fix: add quality tags and an @artist tag, or the Turbo LoRA's stronger default style

pitfalls.symptom: an artist tag has almost no effect

pitfalls.fix: 'safe' in the positive (and nsfw/explicit in the negative), and a longer prompt
describe each character's appearance after naming them

pitfalls.symptom: fried / over-contrasted output with the Turbo LoRA
pitfalls.cause: base settings (cfg 4, 30 steps) kept with the LoRA
